sections.title: 5. Embeddings & Vector Search
sections.body:
### 5.1 Embedding Models — Recap (See §2.7 for the embedding model API.) For retrieval, the choice of embedding model and the choice of vector store are independent decisions. Gemini embeddings work with any ANN store, but the platform's native Vector Search provides the tightest integration. ### 5.2 Agent Platform Vector Search (VS 1.0) Vector Search 1.0 is the original managed ANN service. It uses Google's ScaNN (Scalable Nearest Neighbors) algorithm internally and supports tree-AH, tree-AH hybrid, and brute-force indexes. #### Key Concepts - **Index**: A collection of vectors with a shared dimensionality and distance metric (cosine, dot product, L2). - **Index Endpoint**: A regional serving resource that hosts one or more indexes for query serving. - **DeployedIndex**: A specific index deployed to a specific endpoint with a machine type and replica count. - **Datapoint**: A single vector with an ID and optional user-defined metadata (string Restrict tokens, numeric features). #### Index Creation Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Dev participant VS as Vector Search Control Plane participant Build as Index Builder participant GCS as Cloud Storage participant Dep as Index Endpoint (Data Plane) Dev->>VS: Create Index (tree_ah, 768-dim, cosine) VS->>GCS: Read training vectors VS->>Build: Build ScaNN structure (async, minutes-hours) Build-->>VS: Index ready Dev->>VS: Deploy Index to Endpoint (us-central1, n1-standard-32) VS->>Dep: Stream index to endpoint VMs Dep-->>VS: Deployed, healthy Dev->>VS: Query via endpoint.predict() ``` #### Python Example ```python from google.cloud import aiplatform_v1 as aipv1 # 1. Create the index index_client = aipv1.IndexServiceClient(client_options={ "api_endpoint": "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com" }) index = index_client.create_index( parent="projects/my-project/locations/us-central1", index={ "display_name": "docs-embeddings-v1", "metadata_schema_uri": "gs://google-cloud-aiplatform/schema/matchingengine/metadata_1.0.0.yaml", "metadata": { "config": { "dimensions": 768, "approximate_neighbors_count": 50, "distance_measure_type": "COSINE_DISTANCE", "algorithm_config": { "tree_ah_config": { "leaf_node_embedding_count": 1000, "leaf_nodes_to_search_percent": 10, } } } } } ) # 2. Create endpoint and deploy endpoint = aipv1.IndexEndpointServiceClient(client_options={ "api_endpoint": "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com" }).create_index_endpoint( parent="projects/my-project/locations/us-central1", index_endpoint={"display_name": "docs-endpoint", "public_endpoint_enabled": True}, ) index_client.deploy_index( index=index.result().name, deployed_index={ "id": "docs_deployed_v1", "index_endpoint": endpoint.result().name, "machine_type": "e2-standard-16", "min_replica_count": 1, "max_replica_count": 3, } ) # 3. Upsert datapoints index_client.upsert_datapoints( index=index.result().name, datapoints=[ {"datapoint_id": "doc_1", "feature_vector": [0.1, 0.2, ...], "restricts": [{"namespace": "category", "allow_list": ["finance"]}]}, ] ) # 4. Query import aiplatform_v1.types.matching_engine as me query_client = aipv1.MatchServiceClient(client_options={ "api_endpoint": endpoint.result().public_endpoint_domain_name }) response = query_client.find_neighbors( request=me.FindNeighborsRequest( index_endpoint=endpoint.result().name, deployed_index_id="docs_deployed_v1", queries=[me.IndexDatapoint(feature_vector=query_vec)], return_full_datapoint=False, ) ) ``` ### 5.3 Agent Retrieval / Vector Search 2.0 Vector Search 2.0 (sometimes branded "Agent Retrieval") is the next-generation service that simplifies the operational model significantly: - **No index management**: You just write documents; the service handles chunking, embedding, indexing, and updating transparently. - **Hybrid search built-in**: Combines dense + sparse (BM25-style) retrieval automatically with learned fusion. - **Native reranking**: A built-in cross-encoder reranks the top-K results. - **Streaming updates**: New documents are queryable within seconds (vs. minutes-to-hours for batch rebuilds in VS 1.0). ```python from google.cloud import aiplatform_v1 as aipv1 # Create a Retrieval corpus (VS 2.0) retrieval_client = aipv1.RetrievalServiceClient(client_options={ "api_endpoint": "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com" }) corpus = retrieval_client.create_corpus( parent="projects/my-project/locations/us-central1", corpus={"display_name": "company-knowledge-base"}, ) # Insert documents — service handles chunking, embedding, indexing retrieval_client.create_document( parent=corpus.name, document={ "id": "handbook-2026", "content": {"raw_text": open("handbook.md").read()}, "metadata": {"department": "hr", "year": "2026"}, } ) # Query — hybrid dense+sparse, automatic reranking results = retrieval_client.query( corpus=corpus.name, query="What is the parental leave policy?", top_k=10, search_mode="HYBRID", ) ``` ### 5.4 Hybrid Search — How It Works Hybrid search runs dense and sparse retrieval in parallel, then fuses the results. The fusion is typically a learned model (not just RRF — Reciprocal Rank Fusion), trained on click data to optimize for relevance. ```mermaid flowchart LR Q[Query] --> Dense[Dense Retrieval
Gemini Embeddings
+ ANN] Q --> Sparse[Sparse Retrieval
BM25 / SPLADE
+ Inverted Index] Dense --> Fusion[Fusion Model
learned weights] Sparse --> Fusion Fusion --> RR[Reranker
Cross-Encoder] RR --> TopK[Top-K Results] ``` ### 5.5 Dense vs. Sparse Retrieval — When to Use Which | Aspect | Dense (Embedding) | Sparse (Lexical) | |--------|-------------------|------------------| | Captures semantic synonyms | ✅ | ❌ | | Matches exact keywords/IDs/codes | ❌ | ✅ | | Handles typos gracefully | ✅ | ❌ | | Works well on rare/specialized terms | ❌ (unseen in training) | ✅ | | Multilingual | ✅ | ❌ (per-language) | | Latency | Higher (vector math) | Lower (inverted index lookup) | | Best for | Natural language, paraphrased queries | Code, IDs, exact names, regulatory citations | **Production rule**: Use hybrid unless you have a strong reason not to. The cost overhead is small, and the recall improvement is significant on most workloads. ### 5.6 Metadata Filtering Both VS 1.0 and VS 2.0 support metadata-based filtering. In VS 1.0, this is done via "Restrict" tokens (categorical) and "NumericRestrict" (range queries) applied *during* ANN search, not as a post-filter. This is critical for performance: post-filtering on a top-50 result list can drop effective results to 5, while pre-filtering during ANN preserves the candidate pool. ```python # VS 1.0: filter during search response = query_client.find_neighbors( request=me.FindNeighborsRequest( index_endpoint=endpoint.name, deployed_index_id="docs_deployed_v1", queries=[me.IndexDatapoint( feature_vector=query_vec, restricts=[{"namespace": "department", "allow_list": ["hr", "finance"]}], numeric_restricts=[{"namespace": "year", "value_float": 2024.0, "op": "GREATER_EQUAL"}], )], ) ) ``` ### 5.7 Reranking Reranking uses a cross-encoder model to score the (query, document) pair jointly, producing a more accurate relevance score than bi-encoder embeddings. Cross-encoders are too expensive to run over the full corpus, so they run only on the top-50–100 candidates from the ANN stage. ```python from google.cloud import aiplatform # Use a reranking model from Model Garden endpoint = aiplatform.Endpoint("rerank-endpoint-123") scores = endpoint.predict( instances=[{ "query": "What is the parental leave policy?", "document": doc_text, } for doc_text in candidate_docs] ).predictions # Re-sort candidates by score ``` **Cost tip**: Reranking adds ~50–100ms latency per query and a small per-call cost. For low-traffic internal tools, always enable it. For high-traffic consumer apps, A/B test — sometimes the ANN top-1 is already good enough that reranking provides no measurable lift.

sections.title: 6. RAG Engine on Agent Platform
sections.body:
### 6.1 RAG Engine Architecture & Lifecycle The RAG Engine is the platform's managed, end-to-end RAG solution. It handles the entire pipeline — ingestion, chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval, augmentation, and citation — so you can build production RAG applications without operating any vector database infrastructure. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Ingest["Ingestion Layer"] Src[Sources: GCS, Drive, BigQuery, Web, Confluence] Conn[Managed Connectors] Parser[Parser & Extractor
PDF, DOCX, HTML, etc.] Chunk[Chunking Engine] Emb[Embedding Service] Index[Index Builder] Src --> Conn --> Parser --> Chunk --> Emb --> Index end subgraph Query["Query Layer"] Q[User Query] QR[Query Rewriter
HyDE / Multi-Query] Retr[Retriever
Hybrid + Rerank] Aug[Augmenter
Context assembly] LLM[Gemini / Claude / etc.] Cite[Citation Extractor] Q --> QR --> Retr --> Aug --> LLM --> Cite end Index <--> Retr ``` ### 6.2 Corpus Management A **RAG Corpus** is the top-level container for a RAG knowledge base. Each corpus has: - A configuration: embedding model, chunking strategy, retrieval parameters - A set of documents (the ingested source files) - A set of chunks (the actual indexed units) - IAM permissions (who can read, who can manage) - A regional location (data residency) ```python from google.cloud import aiplatform_v1 as aipv1 rag_client = aipv1.RagDataServiceClient(client_options={ "api_endpoint": "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com" }) corpus = rag_client.create_rag_corpus( parent="projects/my-project/locations/us-central1", rag_corpus={ "display_name": "engineering-wiki-v2", "description": "All engineering wiki pages, refreshed nightly", "rag_embedding_model_config": { "vertex_prediction_endpoint": { "endpoint": "projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/gemini-embedding-002" } }, "rag_vector_db_config": { "rag_managed_db": {} # Let Google manage the vector DB } } ) ``` ### 6.3 Data Ingestion & Connectors The RAG Engine provides managed connectors for common data sources, eliminating the need to write custom ingestion pipelines: | Source | Auth Method | Refresh Strategy | |--------|-------------|------------------| | Cloud Storage | Service Account | On-demand or scheduled | | Google Drive | OAuth or Service Account | On-demand | | BigQuery | Service Account | Scheduled query → export to GCS → ingest | | Slack | OAuth | Webhook-triggered | | Confluence | API token | Scheduled | | Jira | OAuth | Scheduled | | Web URLs | None (public) | Scheduled crawl | | SharePoint | OAuth | Scheduled | ```python # Ingest from GCS import google.cloud.aiplatform_v1.types.rag as rag rag_client.import_rag_files( parent=corpus.name, import_rag_files_config={ "gcs_source": { "uris": ["gs://my-bucket/wiki/**/*.md"] }, "chunking_config": { "fixed_length_chunking": { "chunk_size": 1024, "chunk_overlap": 128, } }, "max_embedding_requests_per_min": 1000, # rate-limit to avoid quota issues } ) ``` ### 6.4 Chunking Strategies Chunking is the most consequential design decision in a RAG pipeline. Bad chunking destroys recall; good chunking can compensate for mediocre embeddings. #### Strategies Supported 1. **Fixed-Length**: Split every N characters/tokens with M-token overlap. Simple, predictable, fine for homogeneous prose. 2. **Sentence-Aware**: Split on sentence boundaries, never mid-sentence. Better for prose with complex sentences. 3. **Document-Structure-Aware**: Respect headings, paragraphs, lists. Each chunk is tagged with its section path. Best for technical docs. 4. **Semantic Chunking**: Use embeddings to detect topic boundaries and split there. Best for transcripts, conversations. 5. **Recursive Splitting**: Try larger chunks first, recursively split if too large. Used by LangChain's `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter`. #### Production Recommendation For most enterprise knowledge bases (wikis, policy docs, technical manuals), use **document-structure-aware chunking** with these defaults: - Chunk size: 800–1200 tokens (roughly 600–900 words) - Overlap: 10–15% of chunk size - Include document title, section path, and page number as metadata - Generate a 1-sentence summary per chunk (using Flash-Lite) and store as a separate "summary" field — this dramatically improves retrieval recall on conceptual queries ```python # Custom chunking with summary generation def chunk_with_summary(doc_text, doc_title, section_path): base_chunks = structure_aware_split(doc_text, doc_title, section_path) enriched = [] for chunk in base_chunks: summary = client.models.generate_content( model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", contents=f"Summarize in one sentence: {chunk.text}", config=GenerateContentConfig(temperature=0.0, max_output_tokens=100) ).text enriched.append({**chunk, "summary": summary, "embedding_text": f"{summary}\n{chunk.text}"}) return enriched ``` ### 6.5 Indexing — Managed vs. Bring-Your-Own **Managed indexing** (default): Google stores the embeddings in its internal vector DB (built on ScaNN + Spanner). You do not see or manage the underlying infrastructure. Simplest, recommended for 95% of use cases. **Bring-Your-Own (BYO)**: You point the RAG Engine at an existing Vector Search 1.0 index. The RAG Engine handles ingestion (writes to the index) and retrieval (reads from it), but you control the index's machine type, replicas, and refresh strategy. When to use BYO: - You need very low-latency retrieval (<10ms p99) and want to pin the index to high-memory machines - You want to share a single index across multiple RAG corpora (e.g., a global product catalog queried by multiple regional RAG apps) - You have a custom retrieval algorithm that needs access to raw vectors ### 6.6 Retrieval & Augmentation The RAG Engine exposes a unified `Query` API that performs retrieval, optional reranking, and context assembly in one call: ```python import google.cloud.aiplatform_v1.types.rag as rag response = rag_client.retrieve_contexts( parent="projects/my-project/locations/us-central1", rag_retrieval_config={ "rag_corpora": [corpus.name], "query": "What is the parental leave policy?", "top_k": 5, "rag_retrieval_config": { "rerank_config": {"rerank": True, "max_results": 5}, "filter": {"metadata_filter": 'department="hr"'}, } } ) # Now feed the retrieved contexts to the LLM context_text = "\n\n".join([c.text for c in response.contexts]) final_prompt = f"Answer based ONLY on the following context:\n\n{context_text}\n\nQuestion: What is the parental leave policy?" answer = client.models.generate_content( model="gemini-3.6-flash", contents=final_prompt, config=GenerateContentConfig(temperature=0.1, max_output_tokens=512), ) ``` ### 6.7 Grounding **Grounding** is the act of constraining the LLM's response to be supported by retrieved context. There are three flavors on the platform: 1. **Grounding with Google Search**: The model uses real-time Google Search results as context. Best for current events, public web knowledge. 2. **Grounding with RAG Corpus**: The model uses your private corpus as context. Best for internal knowledge. 3. **Grounding with Inline Context**: You pass context inline in the prompt (the "manual" approach). Best for ad-hoc context the application has at hand. ```python # Grounding with a RAG corpus (Vertex AI Search integration) from google.genai.types import GenerateContentConfig, Tool grounding_tool = Tool( retrieval=Tool.Retrieval( vertex_ai_search=Tool.Retrieval.VertexAISearch( datastore="projects/my-project/locations/global/collections/default_collection/dataStores/my-datastore" ) ) ) response = client.models.generate_content( model="gemini-3.6-flash", contents="What is our refund policy for enterprise customers?", config=GenerateContentConfig( tools=[grounding_tool], temperature=0.0, ), ) # The response includes grounding metadata for chunk in response.candidates[0].grounding_metadata.grounding_chunks: print(f"Source: {chunk.web.uri}") ``` ### 6.8 Citations & Corroboration When grounding is enabled, the response includes structured citation metadata: - **Grounding chunks**: The actual passages used, with source URIs - **Grounding supports**: Which spans of the response are supported by which chunks - **Web search queries**: The queries the model issued (if Google Search grounding) **Corroboration** is a stricter requirement: a claim is corroborated only if supported by ≥2 independent sources. Use this for high-stakes domains (medical, legal, financial) where a single-source claim is risky. ```python # Check corroboration supports = response.candidates[0].grounding_metadata.grounding_supports for support in supports: claim = response.text[support.start_index:support.end_index] source_count = len(support.grounding_chunk_indices) if source_count < 2: print(f"⚠️ Low-corroboration claim: {claim} (sources: {source_count})") ```

sections.title: 7. Agent Search
sections.body:
### 7.1 Agent Search Architecture Agent Search (formerly Vertex AI Search / Enterprise Search) is a higher-level abstraction over the RAG Engine and Vector Search, optimized for production search applications. It provides: - **Pre-built UI widgets** (search bar, result rendering, filters) - **Out-of-the-box ranking models** tuned for common enterprise search scenarios - **Faceted search** with auto-generated facets - **Recommendations** based on user behavior - **Analytics dashboards** (CTR, zero-result queries, top queries) ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph AS["Agent Search Service"] DS[Data Stores
Websites / GCS / Drive / BigQuery / Cloud SQL] Sch[Schema Engine
auto-detect + custom fields] Idx[Search Index
hybrid ANN + inverted] RNK[Ranking Engine
learning-to-rank] Rec[Recommendation Engine] UI[UI Widget Generator] An[Analytics Pipeline] end User[End User] --> UI UI --> RNK DS --> Sch --> Idx --> RNK RNK --> Rec RNK --> An ``` ### 7.2 Data Stores A Data Store is the top-level container in Agent Search. Types include: - **Website data store**: Crawl a list of URLs or a sitemap. Includes robots.txt compliance. - **Unstructured data store**: PDF, DOCX, HTML, plain text in GCS or Drive. Auto-extracted metadata. - **Structured data store**: BigQuery tables, Cloud SQL, Spanner. Search over rows with schema-aware ranking. - **Faq data store**: Q&A pairs for FAQ-style search. ```python from google.cloud.discoveryengine_v1 import DataStoreServiceClient, DataStore ds_client = DataStoreServiceClient() ds = ds_client.create_data_store( parent="projects/my-project/locations/global", data_store=DataStore( display_name="product-docs", industry_vertical="GENERIC", content_config="CONTENT_REQUIRED", solution_types=["SOLUTION_TYPE_SEARCH"], ) ) ``` ### 7.3 Grounding with Search Agent Search can act as a grounding source for Gemini models, similar to RAG corpora but with the added benefit of the ranking engine: ```python from google.genai.types import Tool, Retrieval search_tool = Tool( retrieval=Retrieval( vertex_ai_search=Retrieval.VertexAISearch( datastore=ds.name ) ) ) response = client.models.generate_content( model="gemini-3.6-flash", contents="Compare our Pro and Enterprise plans", config=GenerateContentConfig(tools=[search_tool], temperature=0.0), ) ``` The model autonomously issues search queries, reads results, and synthesizes an answer with citations. This is the fastest path from "we have docs" to "we have a grounded chatbot."

sections.title: 8. Agentic AI on Agent Platform
sections.body:
### 8.1 Agents Overview — Studio vs API vs ADK The platform offers three ways to build agents, each targeting a different persona: | Approach | Persona | When to Use | |----------|---------|-------------| | **Agent Studio (no-code)** | PM, business analyst | Prototyping, simple Q&A agents, demos | | **Agent Platform API (low-code)** | Backend developer | Production deployment of agents designed in Studio, or hand-coded orchestration | | **Agent Development Kit (ADK) (pro-code)** | ML/AI engineer | Complex multi-agent systems, custom reasoning loops, deep integration with LangChain/LangGraph/CrewAI | ### 8.2 Agent Runtime The Agent Runtime is the execution engine that runs the agent loop: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User / Client participant GW as Agent Gateway participant RT as Agent Runtime participant LLM as Model Endpoint participant Sess as Session Store participant Mem as Memory Bank participant Tools as Tool Layer (MCP/Function) participant Retr as RAG / Vector Search U->>GW: Send message to agent GW->>RT: Dispatch to agent revision RT->>Sess: Load session state RT->>Mem: Load relevant long-term memory RT->>Retr: Optional: retrieve context loop Agent Loop (max N iterations) RT->>LLM: Generate next step LLM-->>RT: Text OR tool_call alt tool_call RT->>Tools: Execute tool (with timeout) Tools-->>RT: Tool result RT->>Sess: Persist intermediate state else final answer RT->>Mem: Save learned facts to memory RT-->>GW: Final answer end end GW-->>U: Response + citations + trace ``` ### 8.3 Agent Gateway The Agent Gateway is the production front-door for agents. It provides: - **Authentication**: Validates OAuth tokens, API keys, or service account credentials - **Authorization**: Checks IAM roles (`roles/aiplatform.agentUser`, custom roles) - **Quota & Rate Limiting**: Per-caller, per-agent, per-region - **Traffic Splitting**: Routes a percentage of traffic to a specific agent revision (for canary deploys) - **Telemetry**: OpenTelemetry-compatible traces, metrics, structured logs - **Circuit Breaking**: If an agent revision's error rate exceeds threshold, automatically route to the previous stable revision ```python # Calling an agent via the gateway import requests headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"} resp = requests.post( "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/agents/my-agent:streamQuery", headers=headers, json={ "user_input": {"text": "What's the status of my order #12345?"}, "session_id": "user-abc-session-1", }, stream=True, ) for line in resp.iter_lines(): if line: print(line.decode()) ``` ### 8.4 Agent Development Kit (ADK) ADK is Google's open-source Python framework for building agents. It is the "official" way to build complex agents that run on the Agent Platform. Key features: - **Agent primitives**: `Agent`, `SequentialAgent`, `LoopAgent`, `ParallelAgent`, `CustomAgent` - **Tool abstractions**: `FunctionTool`, `LangchainTool`, `MCPTool`, `OpenAPITool` - **Session & Memory**: Pluggable backends (in-memory, Vertex AI Sessions, Cloud SQL) - **Code execution**: Sandboxed Python execution built-in - **Built-in eval**: Run agent test suites as part of CI ```python from google.adk import Agent, Runner, Session, Memory from google.adk.tools import function_tool, MCPTool from google.adk.sessions import VertexSessionService from google.adk.memory import VertexMemoryService # Define tools @function_tool def get_order_status(order_id: str) -> dict: """Look up order status by ID.""" # ... call order service ... return {"order_id": order_id, "status": "shipped", "eta": "2026-08-09"} @function_tool def issue_refund(order_id: str, amount: float) -> dict: """Issue a refund for an order.""" # ... call billing service ... return {"refund_id": "r-123", "status": "processed"} # Create the agent agent = Agent( name="customer-support-agent", model="gemini-3.6-flash", description="Handles customer order and refund inquiries", instruction="""You are a customer support agent. 1. Always identify the order ID first. 2. Look up status before promising refunds. 3. Issue refunds only for orders with status 'shipped' or 'delayed'. 4. Be concise and cite policies.""", tools=[get_order_status, issue_refund], ) # Wire up sessions and memory session_service = VertexSessionService( project="my-project", location="us-central1" ) memory_service = VertexMemoryService( project="my-project", location="us-central1" ) runner = Runner( agent=agent, session_service=session_service, memory_service=memory_service, ) # Run a turn import asyncio async def chat(): session = await session_service.create_session(user_id="user-abc") response = await runner.run_async( user_id="user-abc", session_id=session.id, new_message="Where is my order 12345? It's late.", ) async for event in response: print(event.content) asyncio.run(chat()) ``` ### 8.5 Sessions A **Session** is a stateful conversation between a user and an agent. It includes: - The message history - Arbitrary state (key/value pairs the agent can read/write) - A TTL (auto-expire after inactivity) - Association with a specific user ID and agent revision ```python from google.adk.sessions import VertexSessionService ss = VertexSessionService(project="my-project", location="us-central1") # Create session = await ss.create_session( user_id="user-abc", state={"preferred_language": "en", "tier": "enterprise"} ) # Update state mid-conversation await ss.update_session_state( session_id=session.id, updates={"last_order_discussed": "12345"} ) # List a user's sessions (for "recent conversations" UI) sessions = await ss.list_sessions(user_id="user-abc") ``` **Production pattern**: Set session TTL based on use case. For customer support, 24 hours. For coding assistants, 30 days. Sessions incur storage cost — set aggressive TTLs for high-volume consumer apps. ### 8.6 Memory Bank The Memory Bank is a longer-term store of facts learned about a user or topic, distilled from sessions. Unlike session state (per-conversation), memory is **cross-session** and **cross-agent**. ```python from google.adk.memory import VertexMemoryService mem = VertexMemoryService(project="my-project", location="us-central1") # The runtime automatically extracts facts from sessions, but you can also inject manually await mem.add_observation( user_id="user-abc", observation="User is a senior backend engineer who prefers Python and uses FastAPI.", scope="user_profile", ) # Search memory at agent-startup time relevant_memories = await mem.search_memory( user_id="user-abc", query="What programming languages does the user prefer?", top_k=5, ) # Inject into the agent's system prompt augmented_instruction = f"{base_instruction}\n\nKnown about user:\n{relevant_memories}" ``` ### 8.7 Planning & Reasoning Gemini 3.x and 2.5 Pro models support explicit planning via thinking tokens. The ADK exposes this via the `planning` config: ```python agent = Agent( name="research-agent", model="gemini-2.5-pro", instruction="...", planning_config={ "enabled": True, "max_plan_steps": 8, "revise_plan": True, # allow the model to revise its plan mid-execution }, ) ``` For more control, implement a custom `PlannerAgent` that uses a strong model to generate a plan, then a `WorkerAgent` that executes each step: ```python from google.adk import SequentialAgent planner = Agent(name="planner", model="gemini-2.5-pro", instruction="Break the task into 3-5 concrete steps.") worker = Agent(name="worker", model="gemini-3.6-flash", instruction="Execute the given step rigorously.") summarizer = Agent(name="summarizer", model="gemini-2.5-pro", instruction="Synthesize the workers' outputs.") pipeline = SequentialAgent(name="research-pipeline", sub_agents=[planner, worker, summarizer]) ``` ### 8.8 Tool Calling & Function Calling Gemini models are natively trained for function calling. The model emits structured `function_call` parts that the runtime dispatches to the appropriate tool: ```python from google.genai.types import FunctionDeclaration, Tool, Schema, Type get_weather = FunctionDeclaration( name="get_weather", description="Get current weather for a city", parameters=Schema( type=Type.OBJECT, properties={ "city": Schema(type=Type.STRING, description="City name"), "unit": Schema(type=Type.STRING, enum=["celsius", "fahrenheit"]), }, required=["city"], ), ) weather_tool = Tool(function_declarations=[get_weather]) response = client.models.generate_content( model="gemini-3.6-flash", contents="What's the weather in Mumbai?", config=GenerateContentConfig(tools=[weather_tool]), ) # The model returns a function_call for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts: if part.function_call: print(f"Model wants to call: {part.function_call.name}({dict(part.function_call.args)})") # Execute the function locally, then send the result back result = get_weather_fn(**part.function_call.args) # ... feed result back to the model in a multi-turn call ... ``` ### 8.9 Sandbox — Code Execution & Computer Use The platform provides a managed sandbox for executing code generated by agents: - **Code Execution**: A Python sandbox (no network by default) that runs snippets and returns stdout/stderr. Useful for math, data analysis, chart generation. - **Computer Use**: An extended sandbox with a virtual browser/desktop the agent can drive (clicks, typing, screenshots). Useful for web automation, QA testing. ```python from google.genai.types import Tool code_tool = Tool(code_execution=Tool.CodeExecution( timeout_seconds=30, memory_mb=512, enable_network=False, # secure default )) response = client.models.generate_content( model="gemini-3.6-flash", contents="Compute the 100th Fibonacci number and explain the algorithm.", config=GenerateContentConfig(tools=[code_tool]), ) ``` **Security note**: Code execution sandboxes are a major attack surface. Default to `enable_network=False`. Only enable network for trusted internal agents, and never expose computer-use agents directly to end users without a human-in-the-loop approval gate. ### 8.10 MCP (Model Context Protocol) MCP is Anthropic's open standard for connecting AI models to external tools, files, and data sources. The Agent Platform supports MCP both as a client (your agents can call external MCP servers) and as a server (your tools can be exposed as an MCP server for other clients). ```mermaid flowchart LR Agent[Gemini Agent] -->|MCP client| MCP[MCP Server
filesystem, git, db, etc.] MCP --> Tool1[read_file] MCP --> Tool2[git_log] MCP --> Tool3[query_db] ExternalAgent[External Agent
Claude, Cursor, etc.] -->|MCP client| MyMCP[My MCP Server
exposing my tools] MyMCP --> MyTool1[internal API] MyMCP --> MyTool2[internal data] ``` ```python from google.adk.tools import MCPTool from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client # Connect to an external MCP server async with streamablehttp_client("https://mcp.github.com/sse") as (read, write, _): mcp_tool = await MCPTool.from_server( connection_params=("github-mcp", read, write), ) agent = Agent( name="dev-assistant", model="gemini-3.6-flash", tools=[mcp_tool], instruction="Help the user with GitHub operations.", ) ``` ### 8.11 A2A (Agent-to-Agent Protocol) A2A is Google's open protocol for agents to communicate with each other, even across different frameworks (an ADK agent talking to a LangGraph agent talking to a CrewAI agent). Built on JSON-RPC over HTTP with SSE for streaming. Key concepts: - **Agent Card**: A standardized JSON manifest advertising an agent's capabilities, endpoint, auth requirements - **Task**: A unit of work delegated to another agent (with lifecycle: submitted, working, completed, failed) - **Artifact**: The output of a task (text, file, structured data) ```python from google.adk.a2a import A2AClient, AgentCard # Discover another agent client = A2AClient("https://billing-agent.myorg.com/a2a") card: AgentCard = await client.get_agent_card() print(card.skills) # what can this agent do? # Delegate a task task = await client.send_task({ "prompt": "Generate the Q3 invoice for customer Acme Corp", "session_id": "session-xyz", }) # Stream updates async for update in client.subscribe_to_task(task.id): print(update.state, update.artifacts) ``` ### 8.12 Multi-Agent Systems The ADK supports several multi-agent topologies: ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Sequential["Sequential Pipeline"] S1[Planner] --> S2[Researcher] --> S3[Writer] end subgraph Parallel["Parallel Fan-out/Fan-in"] P1[Coordinator] --> P2[Search Agent] P1 --> P3[DB Agent] P1 --> P4[Calc Agent] P2 --> P5[Synthesizer] P3 --> P5 P4 --> P5 end subgraph Hierarchical["Hierarchical / Orchestrator-Worker"] H1[Orchestrator] --> H2[Specialist A] H1 --> H3[Specialist B] H1 --> H4[Specialist C] end subgraph Loop["Loop / Iterative Refinement"] L1[Generator] --> L2[Critic] L2 -->|revise| L1 L2 -->|accept| L3[Final] end ``` ```python from google.adk import SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent, Agent # Example: hierarchical customer support triage = Agent(name="triage", model="gemini-3.6-flash", instruction="Classify the issue type.") billing_specialist = Agent(name="billing", model="gemini-3.6-flash", tools=[...], instruction="...") tech_specialist = Agent(name="tech", model="gemini-3.6-flash", tools=[...], instruction="...") escalation = Agent(name="escalation", model="gemini-2.5-pro", instruction="Handle escalations to humans.") system = SequentialAgent( name="support-system", sub_agents=[triage, ParallelAgent(sub_agents=[billing_specialist, tech_specialist]), escalation], ) ```
